slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content: Loir River Whites — This course covers Jasnières, Coteaux-du-Loir (white), Coteaux-du-Vendômois (white), Orléans (white), and Touraine (white), exploring the geography, soils, varieties, and stylistic characteristics of each AOC. Note: The Loir River is a tributary of the Loire — without the final "e."
slides.1.title: Loir River Whites
slides.1.content:
This course systematically explores the terroir characteristics of Jasnières, Coteaux-du-Loir (white), Coteaux-du-Vendômois (white), Orléans (white), and Touraine (white), helping you build a solid knowledge framework for the Loire Valley.

Through systematic study, you will be able to identify the typical styles of these AOCs and accurately describe their characteristics during tasting.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which of the following AOCs is covered in this course?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Jasnières is a small but prestigious AOC on the Loir River (a tributary without the final "e"), producing 100% Chenin Blanc dry whites. Located in the Sarthe department, it represents the northernmost extreme for serious dry Chenin Blanc in the Loire system, with a notably high-acid, mineral style in cool vintages.
